definition: A normalization technique that normalizes activations across the features of a single training example rather than across a batch.
details: Layer normalization is widely used in transformer architectures because it works well with variable sequence lengths and small batch sizes, unlike batch normalization.
story: Think of an orchestra warming up: no single instrument carries the piece, but together they make the sound. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. The layout decides what the machine can even attempt, before it learns a single thing. The shape of the machine is half the idea. That blueprint is Layer Normalization.
